questions.prompt: You've deployed an e- commerce website using Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website domain name is myshoppingweb.com.Your client requires that customers can access the site using both: myshoppingweb.com (the root domain), and www.myshoppingweb.com (the subdomain) You are managing DNS using Amazon Route 53. Which configuration should you set up in Route 53 to fulfill this requirement?

Create a CNAME record for myshoppingweb.com and a CNAME record for 'mwv.myshoppingwebcom

Create an A record for myshoppingweb.com and an AAAA record for www.myshoppingweb.com
explanations: The apex record is a CNAME, which DNS does not permit. An alias for www does not repair the invalid apex.
Both records are CNAMEs, so the root-domain record remains invalid even though a CNAME for www is allowed.
The alias supports the root domain and tracks the ALB endpoint. The www CNAME can point to that endpoint or the root name.
Ordinary A/AAAA records require IP addresses; an ALB has changing addresses and should be targeted with aliases or a valid subdomain CNAME.

The application only needs to acknowledge when it has accepted a request, not when it has processed it. Initially, the application failed to meet acceptance criteria due to numerous throttling errors during data processing. To resolve this issue, the company had to raise the default number of Lambda concurrent executions several times. How can a solutions architect improve the scalability of the infrastructure to reduce throttling errors?
options: Rewrite the Lambda function code into a Go application that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use native Go drivers for database connection.

Rewrite the Lambda function code into 2 functions - one function to receive the information and another function to persist the information into the database. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to signal available work to the second Lambda function.

Migrate the data store from Aurora to Amazon DynamoDB. Set up a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster between the application and the DynamoDB database. Configure the application to route DynamoDB requests to the DAX cluster using the DAX client SDK.

Rewrite the Lambda function code into 2 functions - one function to receive the information and another function to persist the information into the database. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to signal available work to the second Lambda function.
explanations: Rewriting to a host/language changes operations without durably buffering burst demand.
SNS asynchronous push/retries do not provide the same explicit queue backlog/controlled poll-consumption behavior.
A complete database/cache redesign is unnecessary for the admission/worker-throttling problem.
Separate ingress and worker functions with SQS, then configure worker concurrency/batching to protect Aurora.
questions.takeaway: Acknowledge a request after durable queue admission, then process it at a bounded database-safe rate.
questions.note: The acceptance function must actually enqueue successfully before acknowledging. SQS delivery is at-least-once; use idempotent writes and DLQ/redrive policies.

explanations: A Glacier-class transition is supported for appropriate cold data, accepting its restore tradeoffs.
Standard-IA is a supported lower-cost millisecond-access class for long-lived infrequent data.
EBS snapshots are recovery artifacts, not simply a different class of globally shared application objects.
EFS lifecycle thresholds are access-based supported settings, not the specified generic two-year S3 object transition.
RAID 0 increases a block-device failure surface and DLM snapshots do not implement the requested object storage-class lifecycle.

questions.note: Choose the class based on retrieval requirements and minimum-duration economics, not age alone.
